extractions.value: Clinical features (progressive muscle stiffness, stimulus-induced spasms, rock-like hardness of abdominal and paraspinal muscles, exaggerated lumbar lordosis); elevated serum islet-cell cytoplasmic antibodies; EMG continuous motor unit activity abolished by diazepam; absence of myokymia or myotonia.
extractions.quote: Our patient had slowly progressive muscle stiffness with superimposed stimulus-induced muscle spasms. The pertinent clinical finding was the rock-like hardness of abdominal and paraspinal muscles on palpation, and exaggerated lumbar lordosis. Serum islet-cell cytoplasmic antibodies were elevated. EMG revealed continuous motor unit activity in the absence of volitional contraction of muscles. The administration of diazepam abolished this activity. There was no myokymia or myotonia. Thus, the history, clinical presentation, laboratory, and EMG findings were consistent with a diagnosis of SPS.
